proposals.description: A Belief within skeptic discourse that compiles empirical evidence of systematic bias, discrimination, and structural harms in AI systems. Encompasses: Algorithmic discrimination against protected groups, gender-specific risk exposure, human-cognitive bias propagation into AI, design choice-driven bias, organizational siloing effects, adverse impact measurement limitations, and the erasure of non-Western knowledge systems in digital platforms. Focuses on how AI systems reproduce and amplify existing social inequities through their design, training, and deployment. Excludes: epistemic, data-integrity, and privacy harms of AI (skp-beliefs-095); capability/understanding skepticism (skp-beliefs-210); and the normative remedies that address bias — this node compiles empirical evidence of discriminatory and structural-inequity harms, not informational harms or interventions.
proposals.rationale: t/2754 backfill Excludes genus-differentia clause (leaf-node tail; gate recall + excludes-veto)

proposals.description: A Belief within skeptic discourse that documents how AI systems degrade data quality, compromise privacy, and create information asymmetries. Encompasses: AI-generated content contaminating training data and public discourse, inherent privacy vulnerabilities in large language models, power imbalances between AI developers and affected communities, and methodological limitations in bias detection. Focuses on the epistemic and informational harms of AI rather than direct discriminatory outcomes. Excludes: direct discriminatory or protected-group bias outcomes (skp-beliefs-094); and the technical measurement methodology for detecting these harms (skp-beliefs-215) — this node documents epistemic, data-integrity, and privacy harms, not discriminatory outcomes or evaluation methods.
proposals.rationale: t/2754 backfill Excludes genus-differentia clause (leaf-node tail; gate recall + excludes-veto)

proposals.description: A design approach for privacy tools that prioritizes the translation of complex technical findings into non-technical, actionable warnings for end users. This approach addresses the 'transparency gap' where users are overwhelmed by technical disclosures. It focuses on empowering users to make informed decisions during app installation. Excludes: technical privacy-enhancing mechanisms themselves (encryption, differential privacy, on-device processing) and blanket transparency/disclosure mandates — this node seeks user-facing plain-language translation of privacy findings into actionable installation-time warnings, not the underlying protections or general transparency law.
proposals.rationale: t/2754 backfill Excludes genus-differentia clause (leaf-node tail; gate recall + excludes-veto)

proposals.description: A Belief within skeptic discourse that the systemic inability to quickly assess exposure across complex supply chains forces organizations into inefficient, large-scale parallel triage. Excludes: general supply-chain security or third-party-risk beliefs, and the tooling proposals that would remediate the inefficiency — this node asserts specifically that the inability to rapidly assess cross-supply-chain exposure forces inefficient large-scale parallel triage.
